items.title:
AGENT HARNESSES ARE THE NEW GPT WRAPPERS

What exactly is an agent harness? A harness does 4 things:

1. Runs the model
items.content:
AGENT HARNESSES ARE THE NEW GPT WRAPPERS

What exactly is an agent harness? A harness does 4 things:

1. Runs the model in a loop so it keeps working step after step instead of answering once and stopping.

2. Gives it hands to read files, call tools, open portals, and run code.

3. Manages its memory so hour three of a job still knows what happened on hour one.

4. Enforces the rules about what it can touch and when it has to stop and ask a human.

WHY IT'S INTERESTING

- The market is MEGA. I think about it like a wrapper let you sell software ($800B market) but a harness lets you sell the work ($5T+ market)!

- It doesn't depend on any one company's model. The knowledge about the job lives in the harness, so you can run GPT today, Claude next month, an open model like Google Gemma, Qwen, Deepseek etc on your own machine after that, and it keeps working. A wrapper was one model doing everything and a harness is a router.

- It gets better the more you use it. See, every correction a human makes becomes a rule the harness keeps, so what you have after 500 jobs is a completely different product than what you had after 5. Wrappers only got better when OpenAI got better.

- You can charge for finished work! The harness knows when a job is done, so you can price per claim, per filing, per review, per resolved exception, or per closed month. This helps compete with SaaS!

- Most jobs are just the same handful of decisions, repeated, using the same few tools. That's true for most of the 800+ occupations out there, which is why almost all of them could have a harness built for them. Lots of space for startups to be building.

-The frontier labs won't come for these. OpenAI is not going to learn how a freight claim gets denied in Rotterdam or which prior auth your specific payer rejects. Those markets are too small for them and the knowledge only exists inside the job. They'll keep making the models better, which just makes your harness better which is cool.

- OH, AND really important, you can ACTUALLY build one now. OpenAI's Agents API, Claude's managed agents, Vercel's eve, LangChain harness framework etc. They all make it way easier to build agent harnesses. 

Agent harnesses truly are the new GPT wrappers.

This is just the beginning.

items.title:
$XERIS is one chain, three proofs.

At the center is the triple consensus engine, scrypt Proof-of-Work for block product
items.content:
$XERIS is one chain, three proofs.

At the center is the triple consensus engine, scrypt Proof-of-Work for block production, stake-weighted Proof-of-Stake for leader election and economic security, and Proof-of-History as a cryptographic clock that orders slots. The project’s published runs with 4 second finality and reached 10,000-plus TPS on testnet, and it lists U.S. provisional patent #63/887,511 against that design. The practical pitch is that no single mechanism has to carry the whole network. PoH keeps time and order, PoS decides who is allowed to propose, PoW makes a competing fork. A fork is resolved when one candidate accumulates two-thirds of stake weight, the loser is orphaned and earns nothing. Stake is also the ticket into the mining race, so hashpower is not detached from holders. That combination is why Xeris talks about “stake-weighted mining”. More XRS staked means more validation power and a better chance at block rewards, with instant stake and 7 day unstake described as part of the client flow rather than a lockup maze. Genesis parameters published by the project cap native supply at 700 million XRS, starting with a 200 million token supply and 500 million mineable over 100 years. There will be a block halving every 25 million blocks, or about 3.17 years. 

Privacy and a post-quantum security.

Xeris treats cryptography as a first-class product, not a later upgrade. Official materials describe native zero-knowledge verification in the runtime, including Groth16-style proofs for ownership, identity, and compliance without exposing the underlying data. The Command Center also advertises hidden-amount transfers so observers cannot read the value of a private send. On the quantum side, the team says validator identity, stake registration, block proposals, and transfers can be signed with CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, the NIST FIPS 204 lattice scheme. It also argues that its private-transfer path stores SHA-256 domain-separated commitments rather than elliptic-curve points, so there is no pairing or Pedersen structure sitting on-chain for a future quantum adversary to unwind. Those are project claims, but they are consistent across the website, SDK, and Command Center release notes. 

A full DeFi surface, not a promised one.

Native DeFi is written into the protocol story as primitives, not as a third-party app layer. The published stack includes a constant-product AMM DEX with slippage controls and routing meant to blunt sandwich-style MEV. A bonding-curve launchpad for fair launches, with graduation and LP handling described as contract-enforced. Wrap and unwrap paths so native XRS can sit in pools. Limit and DCA-style order primitives on the roadmap of the same suite. The JavaScript SDK already exposes token creation, pool deployment, launchpad buys, and stake/unstake calls, which is a useful signal that the Xeris team is building developer access alongside the UI. 

Wallets in your browser and in your pocket.

Access is not limited to a desktop node. Xeris Wallet is listed as a Chrome extension for send, receive, swap, stake, and dApp signing. An Android wallet is on Google Play as a public beta, with stealth addresses, biometric lock, multi-asset balances including staked XRS, QR send, and even in-app AI-agent key generation. iOS has been part of the same roadmap, with TestFlight and App Store submissions as the mobile pair to Android, this will be publically available very soon. This matters for a chain that wants everyday users, not just node operators. A Layer-1 can have elegant consensus and still fail if the only way in is a terminal window.

The Xeris Command Center, mine and create.

The Xeris Command Center is the operational client. It is a Rust desktop environment for macOS and Windows, with an Android companion that can create or import a wallet and send on the network. The desktop app is where the “everyone can mine XRS” idea becomes concrete. The base block reward is 10 XRS with halving every 25 million blocks (3.17 years). A light mining client that stays online, verifies headers, accumulates validation power from uptime plus stake, and participates without standing up a full industrial farm. There's a minimum 1000 XRS stake to activate mining and rewards tied to attested work rather than pool politics. For a community that has watched mining concentrate into warehouses, a light client that ordinary holders can run from their laptop is one of the more distinctive product choices Xeris has made.

ARI, the in-house AI model.

Xeris does not stop at ledger software. Ari is the project’s sovereign LLM, a NumPy-native model meant to run on local hardware, with no cloud telemetry and no prompt leakage to a third party. The SDK and Command Center treat Ari agents as on-chain actors that can be registered, budget-capped, and delegated. That is an ambitious pairing, a chain and a local model designed to keep both money and language off someone else’s servers. As a product thesis, it is coherent. Privacy for assets and privacy for inference, under the same company stack.

Real-world assets as the economic target.

The token page frames native XRS as fuel for an RWA economy, especially fractional real estate, biotech pathways, and enterprise assets. The Alexandria protocol is the tokenization layer, Ricardian contracts that bind an on-chain token to a legal document, plus jurisdiction tags, accredited-investor gates, and transfer restrictions. That is the grown-up version of “putting property on-chain”. 

The 5:1 mainnet swap.

Before mainnet launch, Xeris started as a Solana token where is currently still resides. At launch, the published migration is fixed, 5 Solana Xeris become 1 native XRS. The team prefers this clean, secure swap into the sovereign ledger rather than a messy wrap. A native DEX and launchpad are slated to go live with that migration, so liquidity does not have to wait for a later season. Holders should treat any swap ratio as a protocol rule to verify in the actual mainnet contracts, not as a price promise. The mechanism itself is simple, public, and central to how early supporters are supposed to arrive on the L1. clear instructions concerning how-to will be provided by the Xeris team.

CertiK at 88.58 AA score.

Independent scoring is the part of the story that sits outside the website copy. On CertiK Skynet, Xeris is currently listed with an 88.58 AA score and a partial rating. The project page layer 1 leaderboard currently shows it at rank #41. Two audits are listed, the latest delivered September 3, 2026, and CertiK has granted a gold team-verified badge. The score will still move up because the last module is not fully finalized yet. An 88.58 AA mark does not make a chain “safe forever,” and a partial rating is a reminder that modules remain in flight. It does, however, put a pre-mainnet L1 on a public leaderboard with a serious auditor, which is more than most early stage blockchains are capable of. The fact that Xeris is already this high up between billion dollar projects, shows how spectacular this blockchain really is.

Global leadership potential.

Plenty of new chains only advertise their TPS. It rarely happens when a project launches a mining client, a DEX, a launchpad, mobile wallets, staking, an RWA contract model, a local LLM, ZK transfers, and Dilithium keys as a full ecosystem. Xeris is that full stack, written in Rust, with a 4 second slot and a holder-driven mining path. The honest caveat belongs next to the praise. Mainnet is still on the horizon, but approaching fast. Testnet TPS, patent-pending language, LOIs, and a rising CertiK score are promising inputs. If the swap, the DEX, the Command Center miners, and Alexandria assets all land as described, Xeris will have one of the most spectacular blockchain launches of 2026. Xeris has built the full ecosystem with a small team in about 10 months since it's mainnet acces token (Xeris on Solana) was launched. This alone shows the conviction and determination of the team behind it. They are building a sovereign L1 that wants holders to stake, mine, trade, launch, and eventually settle real world assets on one chain. CertiK’s current 88.58 AA score is the first widely visible 3rd party grade on all that hard work. Xeris is not waiting for permission to become a full stack, they have already built the full ecosystem from the ground up.

The next chapter is mainnet, and the foundation already shows it's a blockchain built to last.

10. MCP → Tool and resource interoperability

13. Security → Injection, permissions, sandboxing
14. Observability → Tracing, logging, trajectories
15. Optimization → Routing, batching, quantization

17. Advanced Agents → Autonomous and long-horizon systems

OpenAI Agents SDK (JS/TS) proves the exact thesis we published in our Master Agent Architecture:

Production AI agents are not prompt wrappers - they are a unified four-layer engineering stack

Harness defines what the agent can do
Loop defines how the agent acts
Graph defines how agents collaborate
Trace defines how we observe the execution topology

Execution Topology:
Agent → Tool → Result → Agent → Handoff → Specialist Agent

Here is how OpenAI engineered this into one executable runtime:

[ 01 HARNESS ENGINEERING: CAPABILITY BOUNDARIES ]
- Tools & MCP Integration: Native function tools and Model Context Protocol servers expose deterministic capabilities without bloating the agent system prompt
- Zod Guardrails: Runtime input and output validators enforce strict schema adherence, filtering malicious prompts and malformed JSON payloads before execution
- Sandboxed Workspaces: SandboxAgent runs terminal commands and filesystem operations inside isolated Docker or Unix containers, protecting host environments
- Session Continuity: Automatic session adapters manage conversation state and memory across runs without manual context splicing

[ 02 LOOP ENGINEERING: RECURSIVE REASONING ]
- Action Cycle: LLM parses objective → invokes tool → captures environment feedback → re-evaluates next step until task completion
- Human in the Loop: Built-in interrupt and resume hooks pause execution for human approvals on high-risk actions before state changes commit
- Realtime Voice Engine: WebRTC streaming connects audio input directly to low-latency agent reasoning, executing tool calls live during speech

[ 03 GRAPH ENGINEERING: MULTI-AGENT HANDOFFS ]
- Deterministic Delegation: Instead of forcing one giant model to handle every edge case, handoffs route tasks to dedicated specialist agents (Triage → Billing → Tech Support)
- Agents as Tools: Parent orchestrators invoke subordinate agents as modular subroutines, maintaining clean context boundaries across deep hierarchies
- Context Preservation: Handoff objects transfer task history and execution parameters cleanly, eliminating multi-agent coordination drift

[ 04 TRACE ENGINEERING: EXECUTION OBSERVABILITY ]
- Structured Spans: Every model inference cycle, tool call, and handoff transition emits structured OpenTelemetry traces
- Topology Visualization: Traces reconstruct the causal execution DAG, exposing latency bottlenecks, recursive loops, and silent failure modes instantly

Monolithic agents fail because context windows are not software architectures
When you decouple Harness, Loop, Graph, and Trace, autonomous systems stop being toys and start running mission-critical workloads

Anthropic's Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code:

"We have no more manually written code anywhere at the company. All o
items.content:
Anthropic's Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code:

"We have no more manually written code anywhere at the company. All of the SQL is written by models."

He said it on stage at Sequoia in May. Here is the rest of what he said, in 14 minutes:

→ the model has written 100% of his code since last October. a few dozen PRs a day. one day last week: 150

→ most of his work now happens from his phone. 5 to 10 sessions open, a few hundred agents running, a few thousand overnight

→ the thing he uses most is /loop — Claude schedules itself on cron. dozens running at once: one babysits PRs and fixes CI, one keeps CI green, one pulls Twitter feedback every 30 minutes and clusters it

→ every single person on the Claude Code team writes code. the engineering manager, the PM, the designers, the data scientist, the finance guy, the user researcher

→ on the SaaS apocalypse: switching costs and process power stop being moats, because the model ports anything and hill-climbs any process. network effects, scale and cornered resources still hold

→ his one-year prediction: prompt injection defenses, permission modes, human in the loop all matter less, "because the model will just do the right thing"

→ the parallel he reaches for is the printing press. 10% of Europe could read. fifty years later more had been printed than in the previous thousand years, and a book cost 100x less

→ "the best person to write accounting software is not an engineer. it's a really good accountant"

the harness, in his words, gets less important with every model. the thing that stays is knowing what to build.

Boris Cherny at Sequoia AI Ascent, May 2026. Clip is minutes 5 to 19 of the talk.
